findings.summary: CLOSED. F-21.13-3 now states the whole-object replacement semantics of POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration, explicitly withdraws the administrator-GET-omits-secrets claim, and the derived procedure instruction in the testing doc was replaced to match.
findings.detail: The corrected F-21.13-3 opens with an explicit withdrawal ('CORRECTED AFTER REVIEW (R1). An earlier draft ... misattributed the cause to the administrator GET omitting the provider ApiKey fields. That was wrong and is withdrawn') and then states the true cause: POST {pluginId}/Configuration deserializes the body into a fresh configuration object and BasePlugin<TConfigurationType>.UpdateConfiguration assigns and persists it, so it is a whole-object replacement and any omitted field reverts to its default, while a partial or empty body clears both providers, both BaseUrls and both ApiKeys and still returns 204 with no warning and no activity-log entry. I verified every load-bearing part of that statement myself. (1) docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 9.3 states GET {pluginId}/Configuration 'returns configPlugin.Configuration when plugin.Instance is IHasPluginConfiguration' with no filtering, and quotes BasePluginOfT.UpdateConfiguration as 'Configuration = (TConfigurationType)configuration; SaveConfiguration(Configuration);' - the decisive source, and it now matches the finding. (2) The plugin adds no serialization-level filtering: grep for JsonIgnore|XmlIgnore|JsonPropertyName across src/ArrTags/Configuration/ returns nothing and ArrConnectionConfiguration.cs:22 is 'public string ApiKey { get; set; } = string.Empty;'. (3) The F-21.13-3 evidence is now a live re-confirmation rather than an assertion: evidence[0] records the administrator GET returning both providers enabled with 48-character keys and a body containing both live mock keys, and evidence[1] records a partial POST {"Renderer":{"Size":"Large"}} returning 204 after which only that one field took effect while both providers, both keys and a previously saved 1,572,864-byte limit reverted - and 8,388,608 is exactly the declared default of OperationalLimits.ProviderResponseLimitBytes (src/ArrTags/Configuration/OperationalLimits.cs:95, 8 MiB), so the 'reset to default' claim is arithmetically consistent. That probe is on the disposable abandoned prefix, is labelled post-review and non-matrix in note 11, and deleted its own response files. (4) The in-run instance remains coherent: the L2 command is the empty-body POST, the post-wipe GET shows providers disabled and keylens [0,0], and the L4 save only produced artwork once the provider fields were re-supplied - a mechanism now explained without any secret-omission theory. (5) The L4 observed field's 'VERIFIER ERROR WORTH RECORDING' paragraph was rewritten to the correct cause and now states that the administrator GET does return the ApiKey fields; the false attribution no longer appears in any row. (6) The testing doc bullet now instructs a complete body, forbids the empty-body 204 probe, and correctly records that a GET-then-POST round-trip carrying the whole body is safe. Nothing derived from the withdrawn claim survives in a current-state document; the only remaining occurrences are inside the immutable audit trail (this file's attempt-1 text and the worker's rework record), which is correct. The severity was re-rated from the original secret-handling framing to MEDIUM for a documented Jellyfin save-contract property with a procedure mitigation, as recommended.

findings.area: precision (secondary rationale inside the corrected F-21.13-3 statement)
findings.summary: The corrected F-21.13-3 and its testing-doc bullet conclude correctly that the settings page is unaffected, but attribute that safety to the 'dedicated password inputs' rather than to the full-object round-trip that is the actual mechanism.
findings.detail: F-21.13-3 says the settings page 'reads the whole configuration through ApiClient.getPluginConfiguration and writes back the whole object, using dedicated password inputs so the secret fields are carried through untouched', and the testing doc bullet says 'its password inputs leave the stored field untouched when the operator does not retype it'. The conclusion is right but the mechanism named is not the operative one. src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html:670-673 populates '#sonarrApiKey' and '#radarrApiKey' from config.Sonarr.ApiKey / config.Radarr.ApiKey on pageshow, and the save handler at 749-846 re-fetches the whole configuration and writes the whole object back via ApiClient.updatePluginConfiguration, so the value is carried because the field is pre-filled and the entire object is round-tripped - not because password inputs are write-only. This matters only because the same bullet correctly states one line earlier that the GET does return the ApiKey fields, so a reader could still infer a write-only secret surface. It is a rationale imprecision inside an otherwise correct and already-corrected caution; the operative instruction (always POST a complete body, never an empty or partial one) is unaffected. Not blocking, and I did not require it in the rework because the primary claim had to be fixed first.
